en: Udāna 6.7 Subhūtisutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Venerable Subhūti was sitting not far from the Blessed One, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and entered upon a concentration free from directed thought.
The Blessed One saw the Venerable Subhūti sitting not far away, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and entered upon a concentration free from directed thought.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
And who has well-ordered them within himself without remainder;”
"Having transcended that attachment and perceiving the formless,
having gone beyond the four bonds, one never goes to rebirth.
